items.stem: A code assistant splits a function across two fixed-size chunks, so retrieval returns half a function. What chunking change helps most?

options.text: Chunk along syntactic boundaries so functions and classes stay intact
options.rationale: Correct: syntax-aware chunking keeps meaningful units together.
Comments are not the cause of the split.

items.explanation: Correct: syntax-aware chunking keeps meaningful units together.

items.stem: Which TWO practices keep a code assistant's answers trustworthy? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Retrieve for the correct version or branch the user is on
options.rationale: Correct: version-aware retrieval avoids mixing incompatible APIs.

options.text: Cite exact file and line and show the real snippet
options.rationale: Correct: precise, openable citations let developers verify.

items.explanation: Correct: version-aware retrieval avoids mixing incompatible APIs.

items.stem: After a large refactor, the assistant still returns old function names. What is the fix?

options.text: Reindex on relevant commits and detect stale results
options.rationale: Correct: freshness requires reindexing and stale-detection.
A bigger window does not refresh stale content.
Temperature does not update the index.

options.text: Ask users to phrase questions differently
options.rationale: The problem is the stale index, not phrasing.
